title: Stream handoff and partial-response buffering to honor context deadlines
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem:
The Go SDK streaming API currently exposes a single Read loop tied to the caller's context, but we have recurring customer reports and internal bugs where: 
- a long-running consumer wants to transfer an active stream to a worker goroutine while preserving a remaining deadline,
- partial responses buffered during network blips get dropped when contexts are canceled prematurely, and
- retry/backoff interactions with per-message deadlines are ambiguous, causing either excessive client-side retries or truncated model outputs.

Goal:
Introduce a clear, ergonomically safe handoff primitive and a small internal partial-response buffer that together preserve the semantic contract: when a caller uses context with a deadline/cancel, in-flight RPCs should either finish within that deadline or return a well-documented truncated/partial result sentinel. We want minimal API surface change while preventing common misuses that lead to silent response loss or unresolved goroutines.

Proposal summary:
1) Add Stream.Handoff(ctx) (name provisional) which returns a new StreamHandle object that owns the streaming RPC and captures the remaining deadline at handoff time. The original Stream is explicitly closed for use after handoff.
2) Implement a small fixed-size partialBuffer (configurable, default 4 messages) that accumulates messages received while users are moving between goroutines or performing expensive local processing. Buffer semantics:
   - Items delivered from buffer are treated as already-received for billing/metrics (no double-counting).
   - If the active context expires while items are buffered, the handle returns a PartialResult error with the buffered payloads attached.
   - If the buffer overflows, oldest messages are dropped and a BufferOverflow metric is emitted; overflow does not cause the stream to fail.
3) Normalize deadline propagation so that internal RPC deadlines are clipped to the smallest of: upstream request timeout, caller's remaining deadline at handoff, and rationalized per-message deadline (if set).
4) Clarify retry semantics: retries will not be attempted if remaining deadline < minRetryWindow (50ms); otherwise a conservative bounded retry policy runs once with exponential backoff cap to avoid spurious duplicate tokens in model logs.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Simplicity vs ergonomics: Exposing a handle object adds complexity but avoids implicit context races. Alternative (single-call transfer function) felt less flexible for common patterns (worker pools).
- Buffering size: larger buffer reduces lost partials but increases memory and blurs backpressure semantics. Chosen default small buffer minimizes surprises while covering the most common micro-pause cases.
- Metrics vs user-visible errors: we opted to return a PartialResult sentinel so callers can explicitly detect truncation rather than relying only on logs/metrics.

API compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing Read/Recv patterns remain supported. New API is opt-in; default behavior unchanged until developer calls Handoff.
- Examples and cookbook additions will be added to SDK docs and README demonstrating common patterns: transferring to worker pool, preserving deadline for graceful shutdown, and handling PartialResult error to resume or surface to the user.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement StreamHandle + partialBuffer, deadline clipping, and unit tests for boundary cases (deadline expiry during buffer drain, buffer overflow, handoff after EOF).
- Phase 2 (follow-up): add integration tests with runtime (small simulated latency server) and a canary rollout to go-sdk-0.28.0 users.

Testing and metrics:
- Unit tests: 14 new table-driven tests covering context deadline expiry, buffer behaviour, and single-retry gating.
- Integration: harness that injects artificial pauses and verifies PartialResult propagation end-to-end.
- Observability: emit metrics stream_handoff_count, stream_partial_result_count, stream_buffer_overflow_count, and histogram of remaining_deadline_at_handoff.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature flag gated behind sdk.experiments.stream_handoff default off.
2) Deploy to CI and internal dogfood for 1 week.
3) Canary to 2% of SDK CLI installs and telemetry-enabled customers for runtime-1.20 and go-sdk-0.28.0.
4) Gradually increase after 1 week if no user-impacting issues.

Links and artifacts:
- Design sketch: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yHandoffBufferSketch (internal)
- Implementation PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/1759
- Example snippets (cookbook): https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/go/stream-handoff

Acceptance criteria:
- All unit tests pass and run under 500ms on CI.
- Integration harness verifies PartialResult reaches caller when deadline expires during buffered state.
- No increase in goroutine leaks in stress test (baseline: <5 goroutine difference for 10k streams).

Open questions:
- Should PartialResult be a typed error with separate Unmarshal method for buffered payloads, or keep a simple sentinel + helper? (Preference: typed struct implements error to simplify checks.)
- Exact default buffer size (4 chosen conservatively) — product may want larger for mobile scenarios.
